bibliographic_source_chain.observation: The work index identifies the transcription source as Dostoevsky, Collected Works in 15 volumes, Leningrad: Nauka, 1991, volumes 9-10, and links the Russian Virtual Library electronic edition.

Volume 9 identifies Dostoevsky, Collected Works in 15 volumes, Leningrad: Nauka, 1991 and contains Brothers Karamazov parts I-III. The page identifies the electronic publication as RVB version 3.0 dated 27 January 2017.

Volume 10 identifies the same 1991 Nauka collected edition and contains Brothers Karamazov part IV and the epilogue. The page identifies the electronic publication as RVB version 3.0 dated 27 January 2017.

public_transcription.transcription_quality_evidence: The sampled Wikisource Book I, Chapter I page reports that it has no reviewed versions. This is a transcription-QA limitation, not a legal-basis or bibliographic-provenance failure.
public_transcription.legal_evidence: The Wikisource work page explicitly marks the literary work public domain. This trace concerns the public-domain literary text body and does not assert rights over later editorial apparatus.
public_transcription.publication_evidence: The novel was written in 1878-1880 and first published in 1879-1880; the FantLab work page also records the original journal publication and the December 1880 two-volume edition.

structure.structure_note: The work index exposes an author preface, twelve books across four parts, and an epilogue. Summing the numbered chapter/epilogue leaves listed by the index gives 96; a later freeze must verify the exact text-bearing inventory and whether any book wrapper contributes text before defining a composition contract.

subpage_revision_boundary.observation: A sampled chapter has its own independent permanent revision, proving that the work-index oldid alone does not freeze chapter text bytes.
